title: Application Metrics vs Logs vs Traces
description: Understand when to use metrics, logs, and traces, and how they complement each other to give you a complete picture of your ASP.NET Core application's behavior.

data.text: Observability is often described using three pillars: metrics, logs, and traces. Each answers different questions. Metrics tell you *that* something is wrong. Logs tell you *why* it happened. Traces tell you *where* in a distributed request flow the problem occurred. Using all three together gives you the fastest path to resolution.
What Each Pillar Is Best At

terms.definition: A numeric measurement over time, such as request count, latency percentiles, or memory usage.
A log message with key-value pairs instead of free text, making it searchable and filterable.
A collection of spans representing a single request as it moves through multiple services.

data.title: Recording a Counter Metric
data.content: Use `Meter` and `Counter<T>` to publish application metrics that Prometheus, Grafana, or OpenTelemetry can scrape.

data.title: Structured Logging with ILogger
data.content: Pass named state to `ILogger` so your logging provider emits structured key-value pairs.

data.title: Start with Metrics and Logs
data.text: You do not need distributed tracing on day one. Metrics and structured logs give you 80% of the value with far less complexity. Add traces when you have multiple services and need to follow a request across boundaries.

In ASP.NET Core, you can emit all three pillars with minimal code. The `System.Diagnostics.Metrics` API handles counters and histograms. `ILogger` with scopes handles structured logs. And the OpenTelemetry SDK ties them together with automatic instrumentation for HTTP, EF Core, and outgoing HTTP calls.

data.title: Choosing the Right Tool
items: Use metrics for dashboards and alerts—they compress large amounts of data into actionable charts.
Use structured logs for debugging specific errors and auditing user actions.
Use traces when a single request touches three or more services and you need to see the full path.
Avoid duplicate data: do not log the same value as both a metric and a log message unless you need both.

data.title: Key Takeaway
points: Metrics answer 'what is happening,' logs answer 'why,' and traces answer 'where across services.'
Start with structured logs and metrics; add distributed tracing when service boundaries make debugging painful.
Use OpenTelemetry to instrument all three pillars with consistent naming and export formats.
data.takeaway: The best observability strategy uses all three pillars together, layered on top of a consistent instrumentation SDK.
